column1: # Photon OS ISO permutation matrix - the executable form of ISO-PERMUTATION-MATRIX.md
# Columns
#   id          stable identifier; also the VM name and the last IP octet offset
#   iso_type    minimal | full          BUILD-TIME axis -> selects/creates an ISO
#   poi         2.8 | latest            BUILD-TIME axis -> selects/creates an ISO
#   stig        no | yes                INSTALL-TIME
#   fs          ext4 | btrfs            INSTALL-TIME
#   mode        ui | ks                 INSTALL-TIME (the fifth dimension)
#   ks_variant  -                       ks only: none|selinux|fips|stigpkgs
#   canister    prebuilt | equivalent   BUILD-TIME axis -> selects/creates an ISO.
#               x86_64 default is fips=1 + canister_usage=1, i.e. the kernel links
#               against the PREBUILT linux-fips-canister RPM from the Broadcom repo.
#               'equivalent' links a canister built from the kernel under test.
#               It is two builds: phase A (canister_build=1 on linux only) makes
#               linux-fips-canister-<kernel NEVR>.rpm, then phase B
#               (canister_equivalent=1 + fips_canister_override=<NEVR> on BOTH
#               flavours) relinks and builds the image. Phase A is CONDITIONAL -
#               it runs only when nothing at that NEVR is already published.
#               'build', 'acvp' and 'kat' are accepted by `sharukhan build-iso`
#               but are deliberately NOT rows: 'build' emits a canister that no
#               row installs (linux-esx hardcodes canister_build 0 and is the
#               kernel the ISO boots), and acvp/kat prove something about
#               certification tooling rather than about a PR.
#   net         INSTALL-TIME axis: <family>-<assignment>-<vlan>, all three network
#               dimensions in one column.
#                 family      v4 | v6 | dual
#                 assignment  dhcp | static
#                 vlan        untag | vlanNNN   (NNN in 1..4094)
#               Absent or "-" means v4-dhcp-untag, which is exactly what every
#               row above the n-block has always done - the column documents the
#               status quo rather than changing it. NOT a build-time axis: the
#               network config reaches the guest through guestinfo.kickstart.data
#               and is applied by _setup_network() against an already-installed
#               root, so the five n-rows cost five installs and ZERO ISO builds.
#               An unknown token fails `matrix::load`, naming the row: POI
#               validates only the TOP-LEVEL keys of a kickstart, so a misspelt
#               key inside "network" is silently ignored and yields a guest with
#               no address and no error anywhere. The harness is the only place
#               that typo can ever be caught.
#   doc         the verdict ISO-PERMUTATION-MATRIX.md records (pre-PR)
#   expect      what mission control expects WITH all PRs applied
# doc vs expect is the whole point: where they differ, the PRs are doing work,
# and a run that matches doc instead of expect is a PR regression.
# On mode=ks + stig=yes: the STIG menu is UI-only (stigenable.py is reached
# only from the curses configurator), so a kickstart cannot "answer yes". The
# ks rows express STIG by listing KS_STIG_PACKAGES manually - which is what
# ks_variant=stigpkgs does. This is a genuinely different code path, not a
# duplicate of the UI row.
#id      iso_type  poi     stig  fs     mode  ks_variant  doc        expect  canister    net
p01      minimal   2.8     no    ext4   ui    -           works      pass   prebuilt
p02      minimal   2.8     no    btrfs  ui    -           untested   pass   prebuilt
p03      minimal   2.8     yes   ext4   ui    -           fails      pass   prebuilt
p04      minimal   2.8     yes   btrfs  ui    -           fails      pass   prebuilt

# Kickstart-only failure class (section 11.3). These have NO UI counterpart:
# the security: key is synthesised for everyone on POI latest, but on 2.8 it
# is only present if the kickstart author writes it. fips is never appended on
# the UI path on either version, so s02 is reachable exclusively via kickstart.
s01      minimal   2.8     no    ext4   ks    selinux     fails      pass   prebuilt
s02      minimal   2.8     no    ext4   ks    fips        fails      pass   prebuilt
# Canister axis. c01 was canister=build until 2026-09-02 and never produced a
# verdict, because `build` cannot produce one: canister_build=1 forces
# canister_usage=0, so the kernel that build creates links NO canister, and the
# kernel the ISO actually boots is linux-esx, whose spec hardcodes
# canister_build 0 / canister_usage 1 and therefore ignores the flag entirely.
# A `build` ISO boots the same certified 6.12.60 canister every prebuilt row
# boots - hours spent re-testing k09. It is re-scoped, not replaced, because it
# has no results to invalidate.
# canister=equivalent is the row that proves the thing: phase A runs the same
# canister_build=1 creation path `build` did (so no coverage is lost), and phase
# B links the result into BOTH flavours, which is the only way a guest can
# observe it. The proof is guest.canister_based_on, which must read the kernel
# NEVR under test instead of the certified 6.12.60-18.ph5.
# One row, not several. The canister is a kernel link-time artefact: iso_type
# and poi change the media and the installer, not the kernel (both variant
# patches set the same linux Release), and every install-time axis is orthogonal
# to it. k09 is the paired control - same full/2.8/ks/none row on prebuilt - so
# any difference in guest.canister_based_on is attributable to this axis alone.
# c02 needs aarch64 hardware: fips=0 is the aarch64 default and is not reachable
# on x86_64, so it stays UNRUNNABLE here rather than being quietly dropped.
c01      full      2.8     no    ext4   ks    none        untested   pass    equivalent
c02      full      2.8     no    ext4   ks    none        untested   pass    fips0-aarch64
# Network axis. Five rows, appended - never inserted: identity.rs derives each
# VM's MAC, UUID and IP from the row ORDINAL, so inserting a row anywhere above
# would silently re-address every VM below it.
# Every n-row pins all five other axes to k01's values (minimal 2.8 no ext4 ks
# none prebuilt), so the ONLY difference between an n-row and k01 is `net`, and
# k01 is the paired control. All five share k01's iso_key, so the block costs
# no ISO build at all.
# poi is deliberately NOT crossed with net:
#   git diff v2.8 master -- photon_installer/networkmanager.py   ->   EMPTY
# The network code is byte-identical across the poi axis, so a poi=latest
# network row would re-test the same file at the price of a second multi-hour
# ISO. mode=ui is not crossed either: netconfig.py offers only DHCP,
# DHCP+hostname, manual static and VLAN, and its validate_ipaddr hard-requires
# four dotted decimal octets - the axis is not expressible from the curses
# configurator at all.
# WHY 7 OF THE 12 NOMINAL CELLS ARE ABSENT. These are findings about THIS HOST,
# not about POI, and they are the reason the block is five rows and not twelve.
#  IPv6 has three independent blockers here, any one of which is sufficient:
#   1. /mnt/c/ProgramData/VMware/vmnetnat.conf has `natIp6Enable = 0`, so the
#      vmnet8 NAT device emits no router advertisement and offers no IPv6
#      gateway. (The prefix it WOULD use is recorded there as
#      natIp6Prefix = fd15:4ba5:5a2b:1008::/64.)
#   2. No DHCPv6 server exists on this host IN ANY CONFIGURATION. VMnetDHCP.exe
#      is a VMware port of ISC 2.0 and is IPv4-only; vmnetdhcp.conf declares
#      only `subnet 192.168.58.0` and `subnet 192.168.225.0`. Turning
#      natIp6Enable on would not create one.
#   3. WSL2 runs in NAT networking mode (.wslconfig: `networkingMode = Nat`)
#      and has NO IPv6 stack: /proc/net/if_inet6 holds only link-local
#      addresses and `ping -6` reports "Network is unreachable". The harness
#      itself therefore cannot reach any guest over IPv6, whatever the
#      hypervisor does. Changing that needs `networkingMode = mirrored` and a
#      full WSL restart - a global host change.
#   => DHCPv6 and SLAAC rows are unrunnable here and are recorded as such by
#      NetSpec::unrunnable_reason rather than written out and failed. STATIC
#      IPv6 needs no router, no server and no peer, so it IS testable: the
#      address is assigned, DAD completes, and the guest can be asked what it
#      has over an IPv4 path. That is n02 and n03.
#  VLAN has one blocker:
#   4. VMware Workstation 17 has NO VLAN backing of any kind. `ethernet0.vlanID`
#      is a vSphere PORTGROUP property; `strings` over x64/vmware-vmx.exe,
#      vmnetBridge.dll and vnetlib.dll finds no VLAN/trunk symbol at all, and
#      the Virtual Network Editor has no VLAN concept. Tagging can therefore
#      only happen inside the guest - which is exactly what POI's `vlans`
#      config does - and nothing on vmnet8 will answer a tagged frame, because
#      the NAT gateway and VMnetDHCP.exe are both bound to the untagged
#      segment. Bridged mode is no escape: the only uplink on this host is
#      Wi-Fi (Intel AX211), and 802.1Q over a bridged wireless adapter does not
#      work. There is no wired NIC.
#   => A VLAN row proves what the installer CONFIGURED, never that tagged
#      traffic flows. The oracle asserts accordingly and says so.
# n01  The first row in this project's history to execute the static kickstart
#      path at all: phases.rs pinned `ip: None`, so Network::Static and its
#      gateway/nameserver were dead code. It is also the only row where every
#      network assertion is provable end to end - address, default route, DNS
#      resolution, and ssh on the CONFIGURED address rather than a lease.
# n02  Dual-stack. Proves the v2 `addresses` list carries both families into
#      ONE 50-*.network file and that adding IPv6 breaks nothing on the IPv4
#      side. Fully verifiable: ssh still goes over v4. The cheapest honest
#      IPv6 coverage this host can support.
# n03  IPv6-only: no IPv4 on eth0 at all. A dual-stack guest that silently
#      ignored its v6 address still looks healthy, so only this shape can
#      expose that. Needs a SECOND NIC (eth1, DHCPv4) purely so the harness has
#      a path in - see blocker 3. UNPROVEN: no VM on this host has ever had two
#      NICs. If power-on fails, the row degrades to unrunnable on the c02
#      precedent; install.rs says so in the failure text. It is not a POI
#      defect.
# n04  The v2 `vlans` path: netdev Kind=vlan/Id=100, VLAN=eth0.100 on the
#      parent, exact-name link resolution (_get_vlan_iface_name refuses a
#      wildcard parent). The tag carries a STATIC address on purpose, so the
#      link reaches `configured` with no server present.
# n05  The LEGACY `"type":"vlan"` path - a genuinely different branch
#      (_convert_legacy_config), and the shape the curses UI emits. It forces
#      dhcp4 on both parent and tag, so the tagged DHCP times out and
#      systemd-networkd-wait-online fails.
#      expect=fails, and THAT FAILURE IS ENVIRONMENTAL, NOT A POI DEFECT.
#      This is the one distinction a reader must not lose: s02 is a real defect
#      and someone should fix it; n05 fails because blocker 4 above means no
#      switch on this host will ever answer a tagged frame, and no change to
#      Photon or to the installer could make it pass here. What n05 does prove
#      is that the legacy conversion ran and produced the right files. Its
#      wait-online failure is asserted POSITIVELY (net.wait_online) and excluded
#      from guest.failed_units, so it is recorded rather than hidden - and so it
#      does not regress an assertion that has nothing to do with it.
#      There is no kickstart-level remedy: networkmanager.py writes only
#      [Match], [Network], [NetDev] and [VLAN] sections, so RequiredForOnline=
#      is unreachable from the ks schema. That gap is written up separately in
#      /root/photon-mc/poi-gap-requiredforonline.md.
n01      minimal   2.8     no    ext4   ks    none        untested   pass    prebuilt    v4-static-untag
n02      minimal   2.8     no    ext4   ks    none        untested   pass    prebuilt    dual-static-untag
n03      minimal   2.8     no    ext4   ks    none        untested   pass    prebuilt    v6-static-untag
n04      minimal   2.8     no    ext4   ks    none        untested   pass    prebuilt    v4-static-vlan100
n05      minimal   2.8     no    ext4   ks    none        untested   fails   prebuilt    v4-dhcp-vlan100
